top_level_objectives: Understand vectors as representations of physical quantities with magnitude and direction.
Learn to perform vector addition and decomposition.
Apply vector concepts to analyze projectile motion.
Observe the independence of horizontal and vertical motion in projectiles.
Investigate the effect of initial launch conditions on projectile trajectory.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce vectors as quantities with magnitude and direction, and demonstrate vector addition.
key_visuals: A 3D space with selectable origin.
Two distinct vectors represented by arrows originating from the origin.
A third vector representing the resultant of the first two, shown via tip-to-tail addition.
student_actions: Observe the representation of two vectors, v1 and v2.
Manually drag the tail of v2 to the tip of v1 to visualize vector addition.
Observe the resultant vector, v_res.

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate how a vector can be broken down into horizontal (x) and vertical (y) components.
key_visuals: A single vector originating from the origin.
Adjustable x and y axes.
Dotted lines showing the projection of the vector onto the x and y axes, forming a right triangle.
Labels for the magnitudes of the x and y components.
student_actions: Observe a vector and its x and y components.
Rotate the vector and observe how its components change.
Use a slider to adjust the angle of the vector and see the component magnitudes update in real-time.
Relate component magnitudes to the original vector's magnitude and direction using trigonometry.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the concept of projectile motion and its initial velocity vector.
key_visuals: A 3D scene with a launch platform and a target area.
A projectile at the launch point.
An adjustable launch angle and speed control.
The initial velocity vector, shown as an arrow originating from the projectile.
student_actions: Observe the projectile and the launch controls.
Adjust the launch angle and speed using sliders.
Observe how the initial velocity vector changes in magnitude and direction based on the controls.

scenes.brief_purpose: Decompose the initial velocity vector into horizontal and vertical components and visualize their role.
key_visuals: The initial velocity vector from the previous scene.
X and Y axes aligned with horizontal and vertical directions.
Dotted lines showing the decomposition of the initial velocity into v_x and v_y.
Text labels indicating the values of v_x and v_y.
student_actions: Observe the decomposition of the initial velocity vector.
Note that v_x appears constant throughout the trajectory visualization.
Note that v_y changes throughout the trajectory visualization.

scenes.brief_purpose: Visually demonstrate the independence of horizontal and vertical motion.
key_visuals: The parabolic trajectory of the projectile.
A second projectile launched simultaneously with zero initial vertical velocity but the same horizontal velocity.
A third projectile dropped simultaneously with zero initial horizontal velocity but the same initial vertical velocity as the first projectile.
Comparative trajectories of the three projectiles.
student_actions: Observe the parabolic path of the main projectile.
Observe a second projectile moving only horizontally.
Observe a third projectile moving only vertically under gravity.
Compare the horizontal and vertical motions of the three projectiles to confirm independence.

scenes.brief_purpose: Allow students to manipulate launch parameters and observe effects on range, height, and flight time.
key_visuals: The projectile launch scene.
Adjustable launch angle and speed controls.
The resulting parabolic trajectory.
Indicators for maximum height, range, and flight time.
student_actions: Launch the projectile with various initial launch angles and speeds.
Observe how changes in launch angle and speed affect the maximum height, range, and flight time.
Attempt to predict and then verify the outcomes of different launch parameters.
